Q275.L1t: The least common multiple and greatest common divisor are both defined for any pair of integers.
Q275.L2t: The greatest common divisor of two integers divides each of them and also divides their least common multiple.
Q275.L3t: For two positive integers, the product of the numbers equals the product of their least common multiple and greatest common divisor, so dividing 240 times 24 by 48 gives the missing number.
Q275.L4t: The other integer is one hundred twenty.
Q275.L2f: The greatest common divisor of two integers is always a prime number.
Q275.L3f: Because 48 is already a multiple of the greatest common divisor, the other integer has to be the smallest positive integer, since the divisor already accounts for all shared factors.

Q320.L1t: Particles in circular motion can have both a tangential and a centripetal component of acceleration.
Q320.L2t: Centripetal acceleration points toward the center and is perpendicular to the velocity, while tangential acceleration points along the velocity.
Q320.L3t: The tangential acceleration is 10 m/s² and the centripetal acceleration v²/r is 100/10 = 10 m/s², so the two perpendicular components of acceleration are equal in size.
Q320.L4t: The velocity and acceleration vectors make an angle of forty-five degrees.
Q320.L2f: Tangential acceleration measures how quickly the direction of the velocity changes.
Q320.L3f: The centripetal acceleration here works out to about 17 m/s², roughly 1.7 times the tangential acceleration of 10 m/s².
Q320.L4f: The angle between the velocity and acceleration vectors is sixty degrees.

Q276.L1t: Successive percentage markdowns are a common setup in retail pricing problems.
Q276.L2t: The coat started at a list price of $325.00 and was marked down in two separate stages across November and December.
Q276.L3t: The December 10 percent markdown applies to the reduced November price, which is 80 percent of list, so the final price is the list price times 0.8 times 0.9.
Q276.L4t: The December shopper pays two hundred thirty-four dollars.
Q276.L2f: Retail markdowns are always calculated on the wholesale cost rather than on the list price.
Q276.L3f: Successive markdowns of 20 percent and 10 percent combine to a total discount of only about 11 percent off the list price.
Q276.L4f: The December shopper pays two hundred ninety dollars.
